note: A Sporting Christmas — 10 Years On. Editorial + data for the December series page. Episode titles are placeholders until Cam locks the running order.
title: A Sporting Christmas — 10 Years On
sub: Five teams. Five droughts. One impossible year. Ten years on from 2016 — the greatest year in sport.
cadence: December · festive lead-up · three episodes per team

teams.statLabel: preseason title odds — the most famous number in betting history
teams.story: Nearly relegated in 2015, champions a year later. Ranieri's dilly-ding dilly-dong season, Vardy's 24 goals, Mahrez gliding — and a 132-year wait for a first top-flight title, over.
teams.night: The night: Tottenham drop points at Chelsea, and a title is won on someone else's ground.

teams.statLabel: down in the Finals — to a 73-win team. No one had ever come back. They did.
teams.story: Cleveland hadn't won anything in 52 years. Then LeBron came home, The Block happened, Kyrie hit The Shot, and Game 7 in Oakland ended half a century of hurt.
teams.night: The night: 93-89 in Game 7, on the road, against the winningest regular-season team ever.

teams.statLabel: years since the 1954 flag — and they won it from seventh
teams.story: Injured captain Bob Murphy watching on, Beveridge's boys winning four straight finals — three on the road — to break the AFL's most romantic drought. Then Bevo gave Murphy his medal.
teams.night: The night: 89-67 over Sydney, and the outer at the MCG sounds like Footscray.

teams.statLabel: years without a premiership — the only foundation-era hurt left
teams.story: Fifty seasons, one famous porch light left on. Twenty-four hours after the Bulldogs, the Sharks beat the Storm by two points and a whole peninsula went up, up Cronulla.
teams.night: The night: 14-12 over Melbourne — a first title in club history, held on by fingertips.

teams.statLabel: years of the longest championship drought in American sport
teams.story: The Curse of the Billy Goat, a 3-1 series deficit, a Game 7 rain delay in Cleveland — and then, in the tenth inning, the Cubs actually did it. Grown adults cried at Wrigley for a week.
teams.night: The night: 8-7 in 10 innings, Game 7, after a rain delay that felt like 108 years.
